clue.text: Helped while little girl spread hay

parts.note: as can mean while, at the same time that
sis is a familiar short form of sister, a little girl in the family
to ted is to spread out mown hay to dry

explanation.surface: Someone lent a hand on the farm while a young girl tossed the hay about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread hay' looks like part of the farm scene, but it is the single verb TED, a dialect farming word.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give help, so the past tense matches 'Helped' directly as a synonym.

clue.text: Was compatible with one vice

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one
greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: Someone got on well with a person who had a single bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree with each other match or are consistent, the sense of being compatible.

clue.text: Main problem is raising Irish lad

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from the bottom upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: The chief difficulty lies in bringing up a boy from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it is the noun for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus is a common Irish boy's name, the Gaelic form of James.

clue.text: Opening for cat in South America

indicators.note: in tells us the cat goes inside the abbreviation for the continent

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat flap or entry point for a feline somewhere in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a mouth-like pore or a surgically made hole in the body, so an opening.

clue.text: Writer gets lie disseminated

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An author finds a falsehood being spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a poet who composes elegies, laments for the dead, so a kind of writer.

clue.text: He rejects last of French to abandon resistance

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so this letter drops out of the French word

parts.note: dernier is the French word for last
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The final word of French must give up the fight against an occupier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of French' looks like it wants the letter H; it is a translation: the French for last.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier is one who denies, someone who refuses or rejects a claim, so 'He rejects' describes such a person.

clue.text: Leaving as green is so rough

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golfer walks off because the grass is so uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out or departing, a formal word for an exit or departure.

clue.text: At first Giovanni Bellini suffered bad health

indicators.note: suffered implies the letters have been put through pain and come out disordered
at first asks for only the opening letter of the painter's first name

explanation.surface: The Renaissance painter Giovanni Bellini endured poor health early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-being is the opposite of well-being, a state of poor physical or mental condition.

clue.text: Fine beverages in drum reported before jumble sale

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word for the drum is replaced by one said the same

parts.note: a reel is a drum on which cable or thread is wound

indicators.note: jumble means mix up, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Good drinks are on offer in a barrel, apparently, ahead of a church jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here 'jumble' is the scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ales are traditional cask-conditioned beers, which enthusiasts regard as superior drinks.

clue.text: Discussed and learned about unit of sound

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for learned goes around the unit

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it, so read means learned
a sone is a unit of perceived loudness

explanation.surface: A talk was had and someone was taught about a measure of acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learned' looks like an adjective meaning scholarly; it is READ, the past tense, as in reading law.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue logically with them, so reasoned can mean argued over or discussed.

clue.text: American list has one stone pine

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: An American catalogue includes a single conifer of the stone variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The arolla is the Swiss stone pine of the Alps, so the two names are for the same tree.

clue.text: Responsibility with respect to America

parts.note: on can mean concerning, as in a book on birds
US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A duty owed in relation to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone, a direct synonym for responsibility.

clue.text: One probes the act of developing training

indicators.note: probes means pushes into, so the single letter goes inside the longer word

parts.note: eduction is the act of educing, drawing out or developing something latent
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Somebody investigates how growth happens in learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like it wants I; it is A. EDUCTION, from educe, is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is the process of teaching and schooling, so training in a broad sense.

clue.text: Section central to a part of stage performance

parts.note: Cen. is a dictionary abbreviation for central

explanation.surface: A segment lies at the heart of a piece of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is a scene in an opera, or a dramatic solo vocal piece, so a portion of a staged work.

clue.text: Measure popular in middle of receptions

indicators.note: in tells us the word for popular sits inside the central letters
middle of asks for the two central letters of the long word

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: A popular drink served at the centre of parties and functions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a unit of liquid capacity, so a measure, and also a glass of beer of that size.

clue.text: Plead for most of season to get sow announced

indicators.note: most of means one letter, here the first, is lost from the season

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to seed ground is to sow it

explanation.surface: A farmer begs, for nearly all the cold months, to have planting declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sow' could be the female pig; here it is the verb, to plant seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to plead on behalf of someone else, as a mediator does.

clue.text: Nieces bustle about college getting knowledge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the college letter
to bustle is to hurry around busily, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Busy nieces rush around university gaining learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bustle' makes SCIENE from NIECES, which goes 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Science originally meant knowledge in general, from the Latin scientia, and still means systematic learning.

clue.text: Bob, who rode the Wonder Horse

definitions.meaning: The British jockey who won the 1981 Grand National on Aldaniti
the 1950s TV series about a wild horse was called ... the Wonder Horse

explanation.surface: Bob was the rider of the famous Wonder Horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Bob the rider of the TV horse, but the jockey and the horse share a name and have nothing else to do with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are names: the surname of a famous British jockey and the title name of a TV horse.

clue.text: He arrests most of old troop in escapade

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened troop goes inside the word for escapade

parts.note: a caper is a lark or escapade

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: turm is an archaic word for a troop of horsemen

explanation.surface: A man detains nearly all of a former military unit during a madcap adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: TURM is an obsolete word for a troop; dropping its last letter leaves TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A capturer is one who captures or seizes someone, so a person who makes an arrest.

clue.text: Encourage fowl to eat most of treat prepared

indicators.note: to eat means to take inside, so the bird surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a hen is a domestic fowl

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the final letter of the printed word is dropped

explanation.surface: Coax a chicken to peck at a snack that has been made ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TREAT to TREA, and 'prepared' rearranges that to ARTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them heart, cheering and emboldening them.

clue.text: Scots own name Ian, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A Scottish possession, a name such as Ian, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect nain means own, as in 'my nain folk'.

clue.text: Hamlet was one to condescend, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is replaced by one said the same

parts.note: to deign is to condescend to do something

explanation.surface: The Prince of Denmark was a man who looked down on others, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like a small village, but it is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so he was a native of that country.

clue.text: Flies lower rate flying

parts.note: to dip is to lower briefly, as with headlights

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent off in all directions

explanation.surface: Charges drop as prices go out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun, the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the order of two-winged insects to which true flies belong.

clue.text: Next to East in second team

indicators.note: in tells us the compass letter goes inside the reserve team

parts.note: a B side is a reserve team, the second eleven

explanation.surface: The eastern player sits alongside the reserve squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside means at the side of, adjacent, so next to is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ascetic's actual existence, one not getting old

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, used in philosophy for actual existence

indicators.note: not getting means the letter for old is kept out of the word

explanation.surface: A hermit's real life is one that never ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect living austere communal lives, so an Essene is an ascetic.

clue.text: I leave friendlier parent at school

indicators.note: leave means go away, so the letter drops out of the comparative

parts.note: matier means more matey, friendlier

explanation.surface: I depart from the more sociable parent at the school gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used as slang for one's mother by pupils at British public schools.

clue.text: Scatter presuming they attack

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw in all directions, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Disperse those presumptuous people who are on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Impugners challenge or call into question a claim, so they attack it verbally.

clue.text: England captain once had sentimentality over centre-half

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: goo is slang for sickly sentiment
CH is the abbreviation for centre-half, a football position

explanation.surface: A former national skipper got soppy about his defensive player.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Gooch captained England at cricket; the football position misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Gooch was England cricket captain in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

clue.text: Island king returns to kingdom, once

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king

explanation.surface: A monarch comes back from an island to a former realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel was the ancient northern Hebrew kingdom, so a kingdom of long ago.

clue.text: Proceeding, no press release given, carried out in Rwanda

definitions.text: Proceeding, no press release given, carried out in Rwanda

indicators.note: carried out suggests the letters are moved away and rearranged
no means without, so the two-letter abbreviation is taken away from the printed word

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of press releases

explanation.surface: Mass killing went ahead in Rwanda without any official statement to the media.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking PR from PROCEEDING leaves OCEEDING, which 'carried out' rearranges; the whole clue also describes the 1994 Rwandan slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1994 mass murder of Tutsis in Rwanda is one of the defining examples of the deliberate extermination of a people.

clue.text: Cherished sick user in state

indicators.note: in tells us the shuffled letters go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota, a US state

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are unwell and out of order

explanation.surface: A poorly addict was looked after in a bad condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges USER to URSE; 'state' looks like a condition, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or a grudge is to harbour and cherish it, and to nurse someone is to tend them lovingly.

clue.text: Money nothing more for woolly garment

parts.note: cash is money in notes and coins
mere means no more than, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Cash, and not a penny extra, for a warm jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine goat wool, and a garment knitted from it, typically a sweater.
